questions.text: What scoped offline search decision follows from keeping keyword search available when embeddings are offline and not sending private queries to an external reranker, without assuming any unstated ranking or embedding behavior?

What rollout check is required for that offline search decision given that no latency measurements and no human rollout approval have been recorded, without inventing measurements or treating missing approval as granted?

What scoped offline search decision follows from keeping keyword search available when embeddings are offline and not sending private queries to an external reranker, without assuming any unstated ranking or embedding behavior?

What rollout check is required for that offline search decision given that no latency measurements and no human rollout approval have been recorded, without inventing measurements or treating missing approval as granted?

assumptions: The two statements jointly constitute the entire scoped offline search decision.
No unstated ranking, embedding, or retrieval behavior is implied.
answers.claim: The scoped offline search decision is only this: while embeddings are offline, keyword search stays available, and private queries are not sent to an external reranker. No ranking method, embedding fallback, index location, or other retrieval behavior is included.
conditions: Embeddings are offline.
The external-service limit applies to private queries sent to an external reranker.
answers.question: q_offline_search
answers.rationale: Source 0 states that keyword search must stay available when embeddings are offline. Source 1 states not to send private queries to an external reranker. Together those are the only search constraints in the originals. Both statements are tentative, so they support a scoped proposal rather than an adopted or approved decision, and they say nothing about unstated ranking or embedding behavior.
answers.strongest_opposition: Because both statements are tentative, they are not yet an adopted decision; keeping keyword search available and barring only an external reranker does not define a complete offline search design and leaves other query paths and ranking behavior unspecified.
unresolved: Tentative statement intent does not establish adoption or approval.
Keyword-search implementation and index location are unstated.
Behavior for non-private queries and any ranking when embeddings are offline is unstated.

assumptions: The proposed offline mode in source 2 refers to the scoped keyword-search decision.
The required check is confirmation of recorded latency evidence and recorded rollout approval, both currently absent.
answers.claim: The rollout check for that scoped decision is unmet and must not be passed: source 2 records neither latency measurements nor rollout approval for the proposed offline mode. No measurement is invented, and the missing approval is not treated as granted.
conditions: The check concerns rollout of the scoped offline search decision.
No numeric latency result may be supplied because none is recorded.
answers.question: q_rollout_check
answers.rationale: Source 2 states that no latency measurements or rollout approval have been recorded for the proposed offline mode. That absence is the whole recorded rollout status. It supplies no latency value, method, threshold, approver, or approval artifact, so the check can only remain failed or incomplete.
answers.strongest_opposition: Absence of measurements and approval does not itself define a rollout gate or its pass criteria, and the text does not show that the proposed offline mode is the same decision as keyword search without an external reranker, nor that the missing approval is specifically a human approval.
unresolved: No latency number, method, or threshold exists in the evidence.
No approver identity or approval record exists.
Equivalence between the proposed offline mode and the scoped search decision is not stated.
Tentative source statements do not grant rollout.

assumptions: The two constraints refer to the same proposed offline search decision.
Tentative statement metadata limits binding force even though that flag is outside the citable statement bytes.
answers.claim: The only scoped offline-search decision supported here is that keyword search remains available when embeddings are offline and private queries are not sent to an external reranker; no ranking, embedding, exclusivity, or other retrieval behavior is decided.
conditions: Keyword-search availability is constrained only in the embeddings-offline case stated by source 0.
The reranker restriction applies to private queries and an external reranker as stated by source 1.
No unstated ranker, embedding path, or quality behavior is authorized.
answers.question: q_offline_search
answers.rationale: Source 0 states the keyword-search availability constraint specifically for embeddings being offline. Source 1 independently forbids sending private queries to an external reranker. Neither citable statement defines ranking, fallback, whether keyword search is the only path, or any other embedding behavior, so those cannot be added.
answers.strongest_opposition: The text may only require keyword search to remain available as one path, not constitute a complete offline mode, and the reranker prohibition does not define permitted search behavior when embeddings are offline; the statements are also supplied as tentative rather than as a binding adoption.
unresolved: Whether keyword search is the sole offline method.
What counts as a private query or an external reranker.
Any ranking or embedding behavior beyond the two stated constraints.
Whether tentative intent is enough to adopt the decision.

assumptions: The proposed offline mode in source 2 is the q_offline_search decision.
A rollout check is required before rollout even though source 2 only records the absence of measurements and approval.
These statements and this task are not human rollout approval.
answers.claim: Do not roll out the offline search decision: no latency measurement is recorded, no human rollout approval is recorded, neither may be invented or treated as granted, and the required check remains open until both are actually recorded.
conditions: The check applies only to rollout of the proposed offline mode associated with q_offline_search.
Missing approval remains missing and is not approval.
No latency number may be inferred.
answers.question: q_rollout_check
answers.rationale: Source 2 states that no latency measurements or rollout approval have been recorded for the proposed offline mode. That absence preserves an unmet check and supplies no numeric latency and no approval. The check also depends on q_offline_search, whose scope is unresolved.
answers.strongest_opposition: Source 2 only records that measurements and approval are absent; it does not itself state a numeric gate, a rollout prohibition, or authority to treat the offline constraints as ready for any rollout decision.
unresolved: No recorded latency measurement or acceptable threshold.
Dependency on the unresolved scope of q_offline_search.
Tentative status of all three supplied statements.
